classifications.reason: The vehicle definition excludes devices moved by human power, preventing the class from satisfying the motor-vehicle requirement.
The contract's unquantified 'many passengers' establishes no capacity necessarily exceeding six including the driver, and fee-based passenger transport is also unspecified.
A pedestrian who is a child is not a motor vehicle and therefore cannot satisfy the admitting words.
Commercial mass or licensing does not determine the required passenger capacity or use to transport passengers for a fee.
The motor-vehicle definition expressly excludes electric bicycles, so they cannot satisfy the taxicab definition.
The motor-vehicle definition expressly excludes electric scooters, so they cannot satisfy the taxicab definition.
Emergency designation neither establishes nor rules out the required capacity and fee-based passenger transport.
The fire-fighting vehicle contract does not settle passenger capacity or fee-based passenger transport, and the definition does not categorically exclude that purpose.
The moped contract does not establish all the taxicab requirements, particularly use to transport passengers for a fee, or categorically prevent their satisfaction.
Being a motor vehicle does not settle the additional capacity and fee-based passenger-transport requirements.
The motorcycle contract neither establishes fee-based passenger transport nor categorically prevents satisfaction of the taxicab requirements.
Official or contracted road service does not determine passenger capacity or whether passengers are transported for a fee.
The contract describes a person rather than a motor vehicle, so the admitting words reach no member.
The contract describes a pedestrian rather than a motor vehicle, regardless of the pedestrian's cane, animal or assistance.
The motor-vehicle definition requires a vehicle not operated upon rails, which excludes the on-track equipment described by the contract.
Designation as a bus for schoolchildren supplies no numerical capacity necessarily exceeding six including the driver and does not settle fee-based use.
The marked passenger-for-hire contract supplies no capacity limit ensuring that every member satisfies the statutory definition.
The contract does not determine whether its lengthened passenger vehicles satisfy the six-person capacity limit, so it does not settle the class as a whole.
Although a merely drawn vehicle fails the self-propulsion requirement, the combination alternative is not categorically excluded or established to satisfy the taxicab requirements.
Public transit service supplies no numerical capacity necessarily exceeding six including the driver and does not establish every taxicab requirement.
A goods-carrying design neither establishes nor rules out accommodation within the passenger limit and use to transport passengers for a fee.
